agent_vs_you: The tree is the right shape: studio stills edited from the user's photo, three 5 s image-to-video shots, a 15 s music bed, assemble, and two code text-overlays. Two of the three faults were written into the agent's own prompts. (1) The closing still asked klein for 'clear space below for a closing caption'. klein, which the catalogue says 'misspells and invents text', painted a caption ('Ridectarp dehaime bultae dliy') that sits under the overlaid 'Shop now' for the last 3 s. (2) Every still and clip prompt said to preserve the bottle's 'existing label' or 'markings', but the bottle is plain matte black with no label. Asking a model to keep a label that isn't there invites one, and the hero push-in grew a large white 'BMOOY' wordmark around 3–4 s. The agent never sees the photo, only its filename, so it assumed a label. I would describe the product as plain on every side, never mention captions or text space in a picture prompt (the overlay adds the words afterwards), and use camera moves rather than product rotation. The third fault, spoken Korean ('여러분 안녕하세요!' = 'Hello everyone!'), can only have come from the music track, because all three shots are silent. The track's spectrogram shows only steady chord stacks and percussive hits, with no speech formants or gliding pitch contours, and that phrase is a classic speech-to-text hallucination on music. So it is most likely a grader artefact (gpt-4o-transcribe on an instrumental bed) rather than real vocals. Nothing in our system can listen to check either way.

fix: (1) Planner PROMPTS rule: never ask a picture or clip model to leave room for, or keep, words ('space for a caption', 'its label') unless they exist. Words added later by overlay are not mentioned to the model, and a supplied product is described as it is ('plain, no label or text'). (2) Feed the planner a one-line vision caption of each supplied picture in MATERIALS ('product-bottle.jpg: plain matte black bottle, no label, on a wooden table'), so it stops assuming labels. (3) Grader: run a voice-activity or music-versus-speech check before trusting a transcript of a music bed. A lone stock phrase on an instrumental track ('여러분 안녕하세요', 'Thank you for watching') should count as a probable hallucination, not 'speech heard'. Harness: the same audio probe as E24c, run on generated music to regenerate genuine vocals. (4) Make each image-to-video's 'no text' explicit by code when the source is plain.
evidence: bottle-closing.png (640x640, klein edit) has garbled black text 'Ridectarp dehaime bultae dliy' painted at the bottom, and the frame at 13.5 s shows it under the 'Shop now' band. A 1 fps strip shows a large white 'BMOOY' wordmark and small print appearing on the bottle around 3–4 s of shot 1, which the source photo does not have. shot-01/02/03.mp4 are 270x480, 5.17 s, video only (silent), so the only audio in bottle-ad-final.mp4 is mellow-music.mp3 (15 s, peak -1 dB). Its spectrogram (0–5 kHz) shows sustained chord harmonics under 1.2 kHz and percussive transients, with no speech-like formant movement. The 'spoken Korean' is therefore probably a transcription hallucination, and that one fault is probably wrong. The opening and closing overlays are exact. The bottle's shape and loop are preserved. The overall fail is still right, because the garbled caption and invented wordmark are real.
